endonym.gloss: the ones who go with the dust

description.value: Small mobile bands who follow the browsing herds of the dune sea and hold no fixed ground at all, meeting the settled world only at the basin edges and only when they choose to. Everything they own is carried, decisions are made in the moment by whoever is present, and a band that cannot agree splits before nightfall without anybody treating that as a failure. The Consortium has never travelled with them; what is known comes through the salt-basin households, who trade with them, marry into them occasionally, and describe them in terms that field staff have learned to discount. The open question is whether they are a distinct people at all or a subsistence mode of the basin population, and the strongest evidence either way is a set of ferment cultures that ought to settle it and does not.

Pequenos bandos móveis que seguem as manadas que pastam no mar de dunas e não detêm terreno fixo nenhum, encontrando-se com o mundo sedentário apenas nas margens das bacias e apenas quando lhes apetece. Tudo o que possuem é transportado, as decisões tomam-se no momento por quem estiver presente, e um bando que não chega a acordo divide-se antes do anoitecer sem que ninguém veja nisso um fracasso. O Consórcio nunca viajou com eles; o que se sabe chega através dos agregados das bacias salinas, que comerciam com eles, ocasionalmente casam com eles e os descrevem em termos que o pessoal de campo aprendeu a descontar. A questão em aberto é se são sequer um povo distinto ou apenas um modo de subsistência da população das bacias, e a prova mais forte num sentido ou noutro é um conjunto de culturas de fermentação que devia resolver a questão e não resolve.

bodyPlan.value: The same tall-necked plan as the basin households, reduced in every dimension and lightened in the bone, with broader feet and a heavier dust hood over the eyes. The scale is darker and carries a permanent load of fine ochre that is groomed into patterns rather than out. They walk between fifteen and thirty kilometres a day for most of the year, and the very old are carried on a frame by the very young, which is the only fixed obligation the bands recognise.
